The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. ## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ad95a1d59f2771bdab56b9616363d08b8d0cc497`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23343 (body and all seven comments: triage `6156900795`, claim `6180874007`, report `6181056129`, release `6181089253`, retriage `6182029999`, claim `6182603141`, report `6183681130`); PR #23597's body, its 15-file list and its net diff against `main`; the head's check-runs; committed source on `origin/claude/issue-23343-import-account-invitation` and `origin/main`; better-auth 1.7.3, `@better-auth/core` 1.7.3 and better-call 1.4.0 as the lockfile pins them. The checkout holds no `node_modules`, so those three were read from the pnpm store's content-addressed copies of the pinned versions (same bytes, read into scratch; nothing installed, built or run).

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The widening — right.**
- One new built-in key, `auth.account_invitation`, declared in `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/templates/auth-templates.ts` in `en-US`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES`, and spread into `BUILTIN_AUTH_TEMPLATES` (24 → 28 rows; the manifest's `emailTemplates` is that list, so it is registered like its neighbours). The name satisfies the spec's dotted snake_case regex (`email-template.zod.ts:133`); its variable types (`string`, `url`, `number`) are in the spec's enum (`:100`). `packages/spec` is untouched.
- Declared variables are exactly what the runtime fills: `sendResetPassword`'s invitation branch sends `user.name` (always, `user.name || user.email`), `user.email`, `inviter.name`, `inviter.email`, `setPasswordUrl`, `expiresInMinutes`, `appName` (`getAppName()` always answers a string) and nothing else: no `token`, no `user.id`, no organization, no role. The declaration marks `user.name` and `appName` optional and the other five required; `requireVars` (`template-engine.ts:175`, `lookup(data, name) == null`) resolves dotted paths and refuses a missing required one with `MISSING_VARIABLES`, which `auth-account-invitation-template.test.ts` pins per required variable per locale with nothing reaching the transport, and pins each locale's subject, inviter, link (href and plain text), expiry, button, footer and the absence of every reset phrase. Every non-`en-US` row passes its own localized footer to `wrap` (the file header's rule), and the footer is the template's own in all four, so no "if this wasn't you, ignore this" survives.
- Copy: names the inviter (name and address), the new account's address, "Set your password", the link's expiry, and whom to contact when it has expired. No organization, no role.
- Exports: five new names from `plugin-email`'s `index.ts` (`AUTH_ACCOUNT_INVITATION_TEMPLATE`, `_ZH_CN`, `_JA_JP`, `_ES_ES`, `AUTH_ACCOUNT_INVITATION_TEMPLATES`), the neighbours' shape. `plugin-auth`'s `index.ts` is untouched; `account-invitation-marker.ts` is internal and `resolveImportInviter` is not exported, so `plugin-auth` publishes no new export.
- The 24 pre-existing rows are byte-unchanged: the template file's diff is pure insertion (132 added, 0 removed; `wrap`, the styles and the footers untouched), and the byte-identity pin's 24 recorded digests are unchanged in the diff while four entries are added and the count moves to 28.

**(b) The selection and its safety — right, with one residual named below.**
- The link exists nowhere but the callback: `password.mjs:82-86` calls `sendResetPassword({ user, url, token }, ctx.request)` and `:87-90` answers only `{ status, message }`. So `sendResetPassword` (`auth-manager.ts`) is the only place the choice can be made, and the diff makes it there: `readAccountInvitation(user.email, request)` selects the new key only when a marker is read.
- Every HTTP-reachable door carries a `Request`. `AuthManager.handleRequest` runs `auth.handler(request)`; better-call's router builds the endpoint context with `request` (`router.mjs:66`, `context.mjs:23`), so a public `POST /request-password-reset` hands the callback a `Request` and leg 3 (`request !== undefined && request !== null` → no marker) refuses it before the store is even read. In the whole 1.7.3 dist the only caller of `sendResetPassword` is `password.mjs:82` (`requestPasswordReset`); the email-otp and phone-number resets send OTPs through their own callbacks and never reach it. In this repo the only server-side caller of `requestPasswordReset` is the import (branch-wide grep, tests excluded). A server-side `auth.api.requestPasswordReset({ body })` hands the callback `request: undefined` (`to-auth-endpoints.mjs` spreads the caller's context; better-call reads `context?.request`), which is what the corrected comment now says.
- Nothing on the wire writes the marker: only `runAsAccountInvitation` sets the slot, and its only caller is the import's own `requestReset` closure, behind the platform-admin gate. The store is a fresh `WeakMap` per invited row, and `to-auth-endpoints.mjs` reuses an open store (`if (await hasRequestState()) return run()`), so the endpoint and the callback it calls read that same store. With no store at all, `getCurrentRequestState` throws "No request state found" and `readAccountInvitation` catches it into `undefined`; inside an HTTP request's own store (`handleRequest` opens `runWithRequestState(new WeakMap(), …)` per request), `defineRequestState`'s lazy init answers `null`, also `undefined`. Leg 4 then compares the marker's lowercased address with the recipient's.
- Node: the store is async-context-local, so a concurrent public reset for the same address during an import reads its own store (pin ④, measured mid-send; unit pin "a task started outside the store does not see it").
- The store stays open for the whole send on both runtimes: `AuthManager` configures no `advanced.backgroundTasks.handler`, so `runInBackgroundOrAwait` (`create-context.mjs:215-224`) awaits the send, and the endpoint's promise, hence the marked call, settles only after it.
- WebContainer polyfill (`auth-manager.ts:227-250`): `run` sets a process-global `current` and restores the previous value only when the returned promise settles. The marker so survives better-auth's awaits there (webcontainer pin ①). The polyfill is process-global, so a task begun outside the store does read it (webcontainer pin ③), and the no-Request condition is what still closes the public door: a public reset interleaved with an import carries its `Request` and is refused regardless of what the slot holds (webcontainer pin ② and ③). Residual, named for the record: on the polyfill only, a public HTTP reset that interleaves with an import can make the import's own send read the public request's store (no marker) and send the RESET copy to the invitee; the direction is a downgrade to today's behaviour, never an upgrade to an invitation, and it sits inside the polyfill's documented single-flight caveat (one request at a time in dev sandboxes). Not a defect of this diff.
- A user-requested reset: the else branch is the pre-PR block verbatim (`auth.password_reset`, the same `to`, `emailLocaleArg(request, storedLocale)`, `user` with `id`, `resetUrl`, `token`, `expiresInMinutes`, `appName`, `relatedObject`/`relatedId`), the only moving part being `ttlSec` (c). Pins ② (negative control), ③ (after the import) and ④ (during it) measure it.

**(c) The TTL — right.** better-auth mints the token with `resetPasswordTokenExpiresIn || 3600 * 1` seconds (`password.mjs:73`, `||`), and `AuthManager` passes a configured value through unchanged (`auth-manager.ts:1754-1755`). The callback's `?? 60 * 60` → `|| 60 * 60` therefore changes `auth.password_reset`'s data only for a configured `0` (and no other value: `undefined` gave 3600 under both, positive values pass both unchanged): it said 0 minutes for a 60-minute token and now says 60. Both sends compute `Math.round(ttlSec / 60)` from the same expression. Pin ⑤ reads the token's own verification row back (default 3600 s / 60; 1800 s / 30; configured 0 → 3600 s / 60 on both the invitation and a public reset).

**(d) The import side — right.** `admin-import-users.ts` wraps only its own `requestReset` closure (the `authApi.requestPasswordReset` call) in `runAsAccountInvitation({ email: invite.email, inviter }, requestReset)`; `createUser`, the SMS invites, the temporary-password rows and the manager links are untouched. The inviter is resolved once per batch (the `null` sentinel flips to a value or `undefined` on the first email row) from the actor's `sys_user` row (`name`, `email`, under `SYSTEM_CTX`); the address falls back to the gate's `actor.email`, the name to the address, so both declared-required fields are non-empty; a failed lookup is caught, warned once, and falls to the gate's address. With no address at all the row keeps the reset copy and the batch logs one warning, rather than an invitation refused by `MISSING_VARIABLES` and swallowed. Pin ⑥ measures both fallbacks; pin ① measures the mounted route end to end with the inviter as the `sys_user` row spells them, the landing on the set-password page and the token setting the password.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23343-plugin-email-account-invitation-template.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-email: minor`. Right: a new registered built-in template key (Studio-overridable) and five new exports, nothing removed or renamed. The body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, the variables, the exports, the 24 → 28 count and the byte-identity of the neighbours.
- `.changeset/23343-plugin-auth-import-account-invitation.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth: minor`. Right: new behaviour (the import's invitation email changes key; a customized `auth.password_reset` no longer reaches imported users, stated FROM → TO with the one-line move), no export added or removed, plus the stated `0` → 60 change on the reset email's data. AGENTS.md: `Clause-②: yes` takes at least `minor`; `(widening)` is the correct arm (nothing narrows). Both packages sit in the changeset `fixed` group, so the key the import now sends and the template that declares it version together; the coupling cannot skew.
- ADR-0087: neither changeset declares a breaking change (no `major`, no `**BREAKING`, no `!` summary, the three signals `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:675-676` reads), so no disposition marker is owed and none is carried. Right. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.
- The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line on the claim (`6182603141`), the PR body and both changeset bodies is right for a new published built-in template key, as the retriage (`6182029999`) ruled.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations, judged against claim `6182603141`'s file surface (template file and its index export; the `sendResetPassword` region and the marker's own definition; the import's marker; their tests; one changeset per package; not `packages/spec`, not `auth.invitation`/`auth.password_reset` copy, not better-auth, not the catalog reads):
1. The marker as a new module `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/account-invitation-marker.ts` — IN. The claim named "the marker's own definition" without a file; a module beside its writer and reader keeps `auth-manager.ts`'s diff to one import line plus the region, touches none of the ⛔ paths, and lets the four legs be pinned without a booted manager.
2. The keyed-map fallback not taken — IN. The dispatch offered it as a fallback; the request-state design was measured on both the native and the polyfill path, and a server-held map keyed by email would have raced a same-address public reset on Node and needed its own lifetime management.
3. `??` → `||` — IN. Inside the region, matches better-auth's own mint, changes one impossible-to-be-true value (0 minutes), stated in the changeset and the PR, pinned in ⑤.
4. The stale comment corrected in the region ("with the ADMIN's request" → no request at all) — IN and true (see ①b).
5. The pre-PR merge of `origin/main` at `32e03d2fd` (`800afa79d`) — IN. A `git merge origin/main` refresh is the practice AGENTS.md names; the PR's net diff against `main` is the 15 claimed files and nothing of the merge.
6. The updated existing tests in `plugin-email` (render-identity, template-runtime-write, plain-text-faces) and `plugin-auth` (invite-link) — IN, "their tests".
7. Not measured (a real WebContainer, the Studio list in a browser, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` locally) — accepted: the polyfill path is measured in-process, the registry listing was measured in place of the UI, and the dual-build gate is CI's. Scratch probes: none committed (the file list is the 15 claimed files). The commit-trailer form and the card's assignee are the seat's, not a contract matter.
- `open_questions`: none in `6183681130`; nothing to escalate.

Out-of-scope findings:
- (1) A failed invitation email is reported as delivered — a real, pre-existing defect, not made false and not owed by this diff. Confirmed in source: `create-context.mjs:215-224` awaits the send inside a `try` and logs "Failed to run background task", and `password.mjs:87` still answers `{ status: true }`, so the import's `INVITE_EMAIL_FAILED` branch is reached only by a throw outside that catch (an `APIError` such as `RESET_PASSWORD_DISABLED` or the origin check), never by a transport failure. The same was true with `auth.password_reset`; it is a failure-propagation class, outside this card's copy defect. The seat should file it (the report's dedupe words are usable as written).
- (2) `AuthEndpointPaths.forgetPassword = '/forget-password'` in `packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts` while better-auth 1.7.3 serves `/request-password-reset` — a pre-existing spec divergence, confirmed in the 1.7.3 dist (no `/forget-password` route; only the email-otp plugin's deprecated `/forget-password/email-otp` and a rate-limiter prefix match). No code outside `packages/spec` reads `AuthEndpointPaths`; the QA checklist (`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/identity-auth.json:171`, `:962`, `:1011`) already records the divergence and tells runners to trust the live routes. `packages/spec` was ⛔ for this claim, so the diff was right not to touch it; it is a spec-lane card of its own, not this one's.

Check-runs on `ad95a1d59f2771bdab56b9616363d08b8d0cc497`, as found at 2026-10-15T03:33:27Z (39 runs; a second, non-polling read after the first at report time): success (30): Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · CI release & engine gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core (1/6), Test Core (5/6), Test Core (6/6), Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Dogfood Regression Gate, Auto Label, filter, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, The card this PR closes must claim this branch. skipped (6): Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance. in_progress, no conclusion yet (3): Test Core (2/6), (3/6), (4/6).
